comparisons.objective: Distinct: PR-794 tunes a string to 440±3 Hz by turning its fitted key and plucking for tuner feedback; the candidate commissions a shock absorber by unlocking, adjusting, relocking, and validating repeated physical carriage stops.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-794 uses direct key grasp/rotation, one regrasp, and bimanual plucking. The candidate adds hex-key alignment/insertion, setscrew release, tool withdrawal/reacquisition at a rotated socket, collar counterholding, torque-limited locking, and impact-response testing. These retention and tool-access mechanics test a meaningfully different ability, not merely added difficulty.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-794 requires pitch within 3 Hz, a matching held-key reading, both hands clear, a resting key, and a 1 s hold. The candidate requires ≥0.85 J impacts in the stated velocity range, two non-bottoming ≤12 mm stops, no hard-stop strike/overload/excess rebound, and lock retention. Missing rubric details: PR-794 specifies no force, damage, or slip limits; the candidate leaves excessive-rebound, overload, locking torque, and drift thresholds numerically undeclared.
comparisons.reason: Both employ iterative rotary adjustment followed by response observation, but PR-794's permanently fitted key directly changes a virtual pitch relation. The candidate's essential tested mechanism is a separately locked collar requiring inserted-tool manipulation and retained-setting verification under dynamic impacts. That concrete unlock-adjust-relock-and-load-test sequence establishes meaningful physical distinction.

comparisons.objective: Select and install a matching driver bit, power-tighten a drawer knob, and return the tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bit-shape selection, removable-bit insertion, powered screw engagement, drawer bracing, and tool placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Cross bit retained; at least 1.3 mm powered screw feed; knob gap at most 0.2 mm; withstand 5 N; stopped driver released stably in stand.
comparisons.reason: The candidate commissions damping by unlocking and rotating a collar, relocking it, and evaluating repeated dynamic stops. Powered fastening and bit installation test a different mechanism and outcome.

comparisons.objective: Fill a moka-pot base to a safe level and screw its upper chamber on snugly, with some versions also inserting the coffee basket.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled pouring, vessel handling, coaxial placement, repeated regrasping, and large-body screw rotation.
comparisons.success_condition: Water remains below the valve but not underfilled; required basket is seated; top is aligned and turned to its snug range; spill and unsafe handling limits apply.
comparisons.reason: Although both include rotational adjustment and regrasping, this record tests liquid metering and threaded vessel assembly, not set-screw release, damper tuning, lock retention, or impact-energy response.

comparisons.objective: Tune a damper versus inspect a bent tube by seating it in a checking fixture.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key and collar manipulation with dynamic trials versus bimanual level transport and simultaneous four-leg slot insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeatable safe deceleration versus all four legs seated within fixture tolerances and released at rest.
comparisons.reason: Both involve inspection, but they test different physical phenomena and manipulation. Candidate response tolerances remain partly undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Hand-tighten a spin-on oil filter from before gasket contact into the manufacturer-prescribed angular range.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cylindrical grasping, wrist-driven rotation, regrasping, and controlled gasket compression without tools.
comparisons.success_condition: Finish 240–360 degrees past gasket contact without removal, excessive tightening, uncontrolled turning, or leaving a hand on the filter.
comparisons.reason: Shared collar-like rotation is generic. The filter task tests threaded installation relative to gasket contact; the candidate tests unlocking, tuning, and relocking an already installed damper based on repeated dynamic stopping behavior.

comparisons.objective: Bleed air from a brake caliper by repeating press-open-close-release cycles in the required order.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual pedal force, wrench rotation, timed state coordination, and repeated hydraulic cycles.
comparisons.success_condition: Reduce residual air to the scored threshold while never releasing the pedal with the bleeder open; finish with pedal up and bleeder shut.
comparisons.reason: Both use repeated trials and a small rotary control, but brake bleeding tests temporal hydraulic sequencing and air removal. The candidate tests impact-energy attenuation, collar tuning, and retained set-screw locking.

comparisons.objective: Tune a robot-axis damper versus recover a drawer blocked by a clothing proxy.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine rigid tool/collar manipulation and impact testing versus bimanual obstruction compression while controlling drawer motion.
comparisons.success_condition: Energy-qualified stopping without bottoming versus ordered jam, compression, clearance, and stable full opening.
comparisons.reason: The record has no separate spec versions, but its body supplies a numeric rubric. It clearly tests obstruction recovery, not damping adjustment; candidate final tolerances remain incomplete.

comparisons.objective: Install an O-ring over a hydraulic plug thread and seat it square and untwisted in its groove.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled elastomer stretching, symmetric placement, release, and correction of a cocked ring.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring is fully seated and released without exceeding 50% stretch or leaving more than 90 degrees of roll/twist.
comparisons.reason: This is deformable seal installation with stretch and twist damage limits. The candidate is a rigid-body adjustment-and-lock task whose outcome is measured through carriage impacts.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock damping versus loosen a nut with an adjustable wrench.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both demand jaw/key fit and damage-limited torque; candidate adds collar adjustment, relocking, and iterative impact-response evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe impact cycles with retained setting versus specified nut loosening without rounding and wrench set-down.
comparisons.reason: The record isolates adjustable-wrench use, while the candidate tests commissioning of a dynamic component. Candidate rebound/overload/drift thresholds are undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Candidate commissions and locks a shock absorber by tuning dynamic stopping response; pr-125 aligns pipe flanges and inserts locating pins.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires hex-key engagement, setscrew release/locking, fine collar rotation, counterholding, and iterative impact-response tuning. pr-125 requires flange transport/alignment and repeated pin insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe physical cycles within stroke/energy/velocity limits, no hard-stop strike or setting drift, and verified locking. pr-125 scores final flange poses and pin seating. Candidate omits numeric rebound, overload, locking-torque, and collar-drift thresholds.
comparisons.reason: The tested mechanism, manipulation sequence, feedback loop, and endpoint are meaningfully different; shared alignment and bimanual stabilization are only generic primitives.

comparisons.objective: Calibrate a robot tool center point by touching one reference point from four sufficiently different orientations.
comparisons.physical_skill: Submillimetre tip placement, contact-force control, wrist reorientation, and stable one-second holds.
comparisons.success_condition: Four credited contacts: 10–35 degrees from vertical, mutually separated by at least 15 degrees, with tight tip, axis, mount, and hold tolerances.
comparisons.reason: Both concern robot commissioning, but the tested abilities differ: multi-orientation point registration versus mechanical damper adjustment, hex-key locking, and validation of dynamic stops.

comparisons.objective: Purge air from a needle-free syringe while preserving liquid, then return and release it in its rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual barrel stabilization, syringe reorientation, fine plunger force/travel, and careful rack replacement.
comparisons.success_condition: Residual air at most 0.05 mL and sample loss at most 0.30 mL for full credit, with no excessive aspiration/loss and a settled released return.
comparisons.reason: The syringe task tests phase orientation and metered plunger displacement in a reduced-order fluid model. It does not test rotary adjustment retention or dynamic energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Break a scored ampoule neck using a protective opener while retaining the separated cap.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization, guarded tool placement, controlled levering to break a joint, and captive-part handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Confirmed neck break; cap remains fully captured; body stays upright; body and opener are returned and released without forbidden contact or escape.
comparisons.reason: This record tests controlled fracture and captive retention. The candidate instead preserves all components while tuning and locking a damper and demonstrating non-bottoming impacts.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus thread shock cord through a spring cord lock.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine rigid rotational adjustment and locking versus sustained button depression with deformable-cord feeding through a passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe dynamic stops and witness-tested setting retention versus required cord lengths on both sides, continuous button actuation during threading, spring retention, and release.
comparisons.reason: A spring-loaded lock is not enough to establish overlap; the physical skills and success evidence differ. Candidate thresholds remain incomplete.

comparisons.objective: Check engine oil by pulling, wiping, fully reseating, pulling again to read, reporting the level, and reseating.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated guided extraction/insertion, bimanual wiping, visual state interpretation, and report-marker placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Valid wipe and reseat precede the true reading; the correct level is reported; dipstick and rag are returned without guessing or leaving the engine open.
comparisons.reason: The task is an inspection sequence with wiping and conditional reporting. It lacks damper adjustment, lock manipulation, witness-torque retention, and dynamic stopping tests.

comparisons.objective: Set a grinder tool rest and tongue guard to safe gaps, clamp the rest, then start the grinder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine linear gap adjustment, quarter-turn cam locking, bimanual guard positioning, and safe button actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Rest gap at most 3 mm and tongue gap at most 6 mm without contact; rest clamped at least 80 degrees; START only after safe setup; hands clear of the turning wheel.
comparisons.reason: This is the nearest record because both adjust, lock, and actuate machinery. However, it tests static spatial clearances and a cam clamp; the candidate tests a recessed hex setscrew, collar tuning, and repeated energy-dependent stopping without bottoming or rebound. Candidate rubric still lacks numeric thresholds for excessive rebound, overload, and the declared collar-drift tolerance, but those omissions do not erase the different tested mechanism and outcome.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus take an ear temperature.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key/collar manipulation with impact feedback versus probe-cover seating, button pressing, and stable handheld dwell.
comparisons.success_condition: Two controlled impact cycles and retained adjustment versus valid probe pose, continuous hold through measurement, and safe set-down.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective, skill, or outcome overlap. Candidate response tolerances remain incomplete.

comparisons.objective: Capture a reference angle with a passive bevel gauge, preserve it during transfer, and mark that angle on a board.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual passive-hinge adjustment, face fitting, release without disturbing the angle, careful transport, seating, and guided marking.
comparisons.success_condition: Reference faces fit within tolerance; captured angle is retained during carry; the final line meets coverage, gap, angle, stray-ink, and clearance limits.
comparisons.reason: Both involve adjusting and preserving a rotary setting, but the bevel gauge has no lock and succeeds by transferring geometry into a drawn line. The candidate requires explicit set-screw locking and succeeds through measured dynamic impact behavior.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus safely assemble a grinding-wheel stack on a spindle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key unlocking, collar tuning, and relocking versus ordered flange/blotter/wheel insertion, spindle alignment, and nut tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe dynamic stops with no setting drift versus correct stack order and alignment, seated nut, released hands, and no damaged wheel or over-tightening.
comparisons.reason: Generic tightening does not establish overlap; assembly sequencing and dynamic commissioning test different abilities. Candidate rebound/overload/drift thresholds remain unspecified.

comparisons.objective: Install a circlip in a shaft groove and turn it to verify seating; candidate commissions an adjustable shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pliers-tip insertion, controlled elastic spreading, axial placement and seating verification versus hex-key use, collar rotation, relocking and response-based iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring seated without overspread, twist or cocking and verified by rotation; candidate succeeds through repeated controlled carriage stops. Candidate lacks final numeric rebound, overload and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Shared force control and tool use are generic; elastic retaining-ring installation tests a different manipulation capability.

comparisons.objective: Hand-mount the final section of a bicycle tire bead without a lever; candidate tunes and locks a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual deformable-bead redistribution and progressive seating versus rigid tool alignment, rotary adjustment and dynamic commissioning.
comparisons.success_condition: Bead fully seated without lever use, tube/rim damage or bead escape versus two safe repeatable impacts. Candidate dynamic rejection thresholds are partly undeclared.
comparisons.reason: The tire task centers on deformable-object tension management, absent from the rigid damper task.

comparisons.objective: Candidate tunes and locks a rigid industrial damper; pr-1694 rolls puff pastry to a target length and thickness without damaging its ends.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a hex key, counterholding, fine rotary adjustment, locking, and dynamic-response evaluation. pr-1694 uses sustained bimanual rolling-pin leveling and repeated translational strokes over deformable material.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks impact energy/velocity, damper stroke, hard-stop avoidance, rebound/overload, and setting retention. pr-1694 checks sheet length, thickness coverage, end damage, tool release/placement, and arm return. Candidate does not numerically define rebound, overload, drift, or tightening torque.
comparisons.reason: The manipulation topology and measured physical outcome are materially different; repeated bimanual motion and damage avoidance do not establish overlap.

comparisons.objective: Orient and swipe a magnetic-stripe card once through a narrow reader slot, then return it to its stand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Thin-object extraction, orientation, narrow-slot alignment, continuous speed-controlled translation, and reinsertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly one good swipe across the encoded span at 0.1524–1.524 m/s with correct stripe orientation and height; card returned stably without dropping.
comparisons.reason: This tests narrow-slot alignment and controlled one-pass translation. It shares no substantive damper-adjustment, locking, or dynamic energy-absorption outcome with the candidate.

comparisons.objective: Candidate commissions a robot-axis damper through iterative dynamic tuning and relocking; record resets a tally counter, transfers 11 nuts, and synchronizes the mechanical count.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, setscrew torque, counterholding, fine collar rotation, and response-driven readjustment. Record requires reset-knob twisting, repeated key pressing, nut pick-and-place, and count/transfer coordination.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe physical cycles at ≥0.85 J within the velocity envelope, ≤12 mm travel, no hard-stop strike or drift. Record requires a prior steady 0000, all 11 released and settled in the tray, and a final 0011 reading, with any dropped nut forcing zero.
comparisons.reason: The tested abilities and terminal state are meaningfully different; shared bimanual manipulation is generic. The tally rubric is numerically complete. Candidate rubric still omits numeric definitions for excessive rebound, overload, and the declared collar-drift tolerance, but those omissions do not plausibly duplicate inventory counting.

comparisons.objective: Use carriage travel to self-align a floating guide rod, clamp it at the far end, then prove full return travel; candidate adjusts damping for acceptable stops.
comparisons.physical_skill: Crank operation, position-dependent cam-clamp closure and travel verification versus hex-key loosening, collar tuning, setscrew locking and repeated impact evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Rod within 0.12° parallel and carriage reaches both stops without binding; candidate requires non-bottoming, low-rebound stops with retained setting. Candidate rebound/overload/drift thresholds are unspecified.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record because both lock an adjustment and cycle a mechanism, but it tests carriage-induced geometric self-alignment and binding, not energy absorption or damping selection.

comparisons.objective: Install a click-lock vinyl floor tile by angling its tongue into a laid row and lowering it to latch; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-edge alignment, bimanual support, angled insertion and controlled lowering versus hex-key/collar manipulation and iterative force-response assessment.
comparisons.success_condition: Tile joint fully engaged and flat without damaged edges or gaps versus repeatable non-bottoming carriage stops. Candidate dynamic rejection thresholds are partly missing.
comparisons.reason: The flooring record tests distributed edge insertion and latching, not tuning or retention of a dynamic setting.

comparisons.objective: Place two setting blocks, then lower and release a glass unit into a frame channel without sill contact.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual block placement and controlled large-panel alignment/descent; no tool-driven parameter adjustment or dynamic commissioning.
comparisons.success_condition: Glass rests on both positioned blocks, centred and stable, without ever touching the sill. Candidate instead requires two acceptable impact cycles after collar adjustment and setscrew locking.
comparisons.reason: Support placement and collision-free glazing test a different ability from tuning and mechanically locking a shock absorber based on dynamic response. Candidate rubric omits numeric limits for excessive rebound, overload, hard-stop clearance, and allowed post-lock collar drift, but those omissions do not create plausible overlap.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and validates damper response on an isolated robot axis; record installs and snaps shut a personal padlock on an occupied group-lockout hasp while preserving energy isolation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a removable hex key, counterhold, controlled fastener torque, collar rotation, tool re-engagement, and iterative dynamic diagnosis. Record grasps and reorients an open padlock, aligns its shackle through two moving hasp jaws, latches it, and avoids disturbing an existing lock.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires relocking followed by two repeatable, non-bottoming cycles and a witness-torque drift check. Record requires the closed purple lock to remain effective after release under 0.3 N·m hasp-pry and 1.5 N·m handle tests, with strict coworker-lock, jaw-opening, and handle-motion hazards.
comparisons.reason: Both involve safety-sensitive bimanual alignment and latching/retention, but one tests adjustable damping plus iterative physical response control; the other tests through-hole shackle insertion and lockout retention. All eight spec versions were read and preserve that distinction. Candidate lacks numeric rebound, overload, locking-torque, and drift-tolerance thresholds; the record does not penalize dropping the purple lock itself, but neither gap suggests duplication.

comparisons.objective: Sharpen both faces of a knife on a whetstone at a controlled angle, then put it down safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain blade angle and contact while executing edge-leading strokes, reorienting between faces, and safely releasing a sharp tool.
comparisons.success_condition: At least three qualifying strokes and sufficient edge coverage on each face, followed by safe placement; incorrect angles or roll-off strokes do not qualify.
comparisons.reason: Contact-rich abrasive stroke control and edge coverage are meaningfully different from hex-key engagement, collar tuning, lock retention, and impact-response testing. The sharpening simulation does not model material removal, while the candidate's relevant outcome is physical carriage stopping. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift thresholds remain unspecified.

comparisons.objective: Assemble a two-part hook tool and use it to pull a cartridge from a hood; candidate commissions and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-part assembly, hook engagement, constrained pulling and extraction versus hex-key seating, collar turning, counterholding and dynamic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Tool assembled and cartridge extracted without loss or damage versus two safe repeatable stops with retained adjustment. Candidate dynamic thresholds are incomplete.
comparisons.reason: Extraction with a newly assembled hook tests engagement and tensile manipulation, not response-based adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Assemble a drive-chain joint; candidate adjusts and locks a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Aligning chain links and joint components, inserting/retaining the connecting assembly and controlling small loose parts versus hex-key engagement, collar tuning and impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Chain joint completely retained and articulated without missing or damaged components versus two repeatable non-bottoming stops. Candidate dynamic thresholds remain partly unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Chain-link joining is an assembly and retention task, not dynamic parameter commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Candidate commissions damping by unlocking, tuning, relocking, and cycling an axis; record mechanically zeros an unpowered joint by holding a gravity-loaded link on its mark and inserting a calibration pin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require bimanual stabilization and alignment/insertion. Candidate additionally tests hex-key seating, bounded loosening/tightening, fine rotary adjustment, re-engagement after collar motion, and iterative tuning from impacts; record tests simultaneous gravity compensation and pin-through-aligned-hole insertion into a detent.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe cycles within energy, speed, stroke, rebound, overload, and lock-drift constraints. Record requires pin travel ≥26 mm with joint angle within 1°, link stillness for 1 s, hands released, and no joint speed above 120°/s.
comparisons.reason: The shared hold-and-insert primitive is insufficient for overlap: the record ends once a passive joint is geometrically pinned at zero, whereas the candidate must alter and verify a dynamic damping response through repeated cycles and secure the setting. Both record spec versions were read. The record has explicit numeric thresholds; candidate still lacks numeric definitions for excessive rebound, overload, witness torque, and allowed collar drift.

comparisons.objective: Compress retaining legs before installing a cage fastener; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Simultaneous elastic-leg compression, alignment and insertion versus hex-key insertion, fine collar rotation and bounded relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Fastener installed with retaining legs correctly captured and undamaged versus verified dynamic stopping behavior. Candidate dynamic thresholds are incomplete.
comparisons.reason: Elastic snap-fastener insertion tests controlled compression and latching, not adjustment or impact-response control.

comparisons.objective: Replace a ratchet-dispenser cartridge; candidate commissions an adjustable shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Release/access manipulation, cartridge extraction, keyed placement and ratchet re-engagement versus recessed-tool alignment, collar tuning and iterative cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Replacement cartridge seated and dispenser operating without loss or damage versus two safe stops with locked setting. Candidate omits numeric rebound/overload/drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Module replacement and mechanism re-engagement are different from tuning a continuously adjustable dissipative component.

comparisons.objective: Replace a toilet roll on a spring spindle while one spindle end is already held in a socket.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compress and steer a spring-loaded spindle, align its free end with the opposite socket, and release it into retention while supporting the roll.
comparisons.success_condition: Both spindle ends are seated, the roll is retained and usable after release, and the assembly is not dropped or incorrectly supported.
comparisons.reason: Spring-spindle seating is an insertion-and-release task, not iterative adjustment of damping followed by setscrew locking and dynamic stop validation. Any missing force thresholds in the spindle record do not make these objectives plausible duplicates; the candidate also lacks numeric rebound, overload, and drift limits.

comparisons.objective: Seat a robot-controller add-on board onto two rows of header pins without bending them; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual PCB leveling, simultaneous multi-pin alignment and force-limited seating versus hex-key/collar manipulation and iterative dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Board fully and evenly seated with all pins straight and no damage versus repeatable safe carriage stops with setting retention. Candidate thresholds for rebound, overload and drift are incomplete.
comparisons.reason: Both support robot hardware, but multi-pin electronics insertion tests a clearly different ability.

comparisons.objective: Sample a handhole's atmosphere through the closed cover before conditionally removing its bolts; leave it secured if the monitor alarms.
comparisons.physical_skill: Guide a hose through a narrow slot, hold sampling depth and duration, interpret an alarm branch, and on clean air unscrew and place two bolts.
comparisons.success_condition: A continuous 60-second valid sample must precede bolt loosening; clean-air trials require both bolts removed and cleared, while alarm trials require the cover to remain bolted.
comparisons.reason: This tests safety-sequenced sensing and conditional inhibition of cover opening. Shared hex/fastener manipulation is generic and secondary; it does not overlap the candidate's fine collar adjustment, retained setting, or repeated impact-response commissioning. Candidate dynamic failure thresholds are incompletely numeric.

comparisons.objective: Ratchet a tie-down strap taut over a crate, latch the handle, and prove load retention during a deck jolt.
comparisons.physical_skill: Execute repeated full lever strokes through a pawl, close the same handle through its latch detent, release, and withstand a physical disturbance.
comparisons.success_condition: Strap tension reaches at least 50 N, the handle is latched, and the crate stays within displacement and tip limits through the jolt.
comparisons.reason: This is load securement by accumulating strap tension and latching a ratchet lever. The candidate instead adjusts a damping parameter with a collar, separately locks it using a recessed setscrew, and judges two stopping responses. Both include adjustment, locking, and a dynamic proof, but their tested mechanisms and control abilities are meaningfully different. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift tolerances are not numerically specified.

comparisons.objective: Refit a loaded drawer onto roller slides by carrying it above riding height, close it, then pull-test engagement.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually support and level a loaded drawer, clear hidden rear hooks over rollers, lower onto rails, and perform a controlled pull test.
comparisons.success_condition: Drawer must ride level on both slides, close correctly, then reopen 30–80 mm while retaining its load; dropped load or drawer is failure.
comparisons.reason: Hidden-hook rail engagement and loaded bimanual insertion differ from tool-mediated damper tuning, setscrew retention, and energy-absorption testing. The drawer's geometric engagement criteria are defined; candidate rebound, overload, hard-stop clearance, and drift criteria lack complete numeric definitions.

comparisons.objective: Carry a carton of cans whose untaped bottom flaps can open unless continuously supported from below.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain underside support and coordinated grasp during transport while managing a gravity-driven containment failure mode.
comparisons.success_condition: Deliver the carton and cans without flap opening, can loss, spill, or unsafe unsupported carrying, then place it stably.
comparisons.reason: This tests continuous bimanual support of a failure-prone container during transport, with no adjustment, tool insertion, locking, or dynamic parameter identification. Record thresholds are largely outcome-based, but that missing precision does not imply overlap. Candidate dynamic acceptance thresholds are also partly undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Insert an emergency-stop button through a keyed panel hole and thread its rear locking ring; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tab-notch alignment, through-panel insertion, bimanual front counterhold and rear-ring threading versus recessed setscrew access, collar adjustment and iterative response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Button seated and ring advanced to its specified angle/gap, then released; candidate requires two acceptable physical stops and retained setting. Candidate dynamic thresholds remain incomplete.
comparisons.reason: This shares bimanual counterholding and rotary locking, but the essential tested ability is keyed component insertion and threaded panel mounting, not selecting damping from impact behavior.

comparisons.objective: Commission and lock a shock absorber versus shim a door jamb without bowing it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key engagement, collar tuning, and impact observation versus bimanual opposed-wedge insertion with force-sensitive stopping.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe repeatable dynamic stops versus opposed shims snug within 0.05 mm, overlap at least 70 mm, and jamb bow at most 0.4 mm.
comparisons.reason: Both involve force-sensitive adjustment, but one tunes dynamic damping and lock retention while the other creates a static fitted pack. Candidate overload, rebound, and drift thresholds remain numerically undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus release and relocate a mounted camera.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recessed-key insertion, collar rotation, relocking, and repeated cycling versus cam release, retaining-lip clearance, supported extraction, and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Two repeatable stops without bottoming or drift versus released camera upright on a pad with clearance, stability, and no drop.
comparisons.reason: Shared release/retention primitives do not test the same ability; the candidate uniquely requires response-based tuning. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift limits remain undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus open a bottle through a safety loop and rocker latch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-mediated setscrew and collar manipulation versus stabilizing a free bottle while sequentially moving two hinged controls.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeatable non-bottoming carriage stops with lock retention versus lid opening beyond 60 degrees while the bottle stays upright and forces remain bounded.
comparisons.reason: Only generic stabilization and sequential release are shared. Candidate overload, rebound, and drift tolerances remain unspecified.

comparisons.objective: Retrieve and reattach a detached live wrist camera to the robot's own mount, then release it while retained and operational.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinate both arms to align a keyed shoe with a wrist channel, insert to an end stop, engage retention, and withdraw the assisting gripper.
comparisons.success_condition: Camera is seated and latched within 5 mm and 5 degrees, continues delivering live frames, and remains retained for two seconds after release.
comparisons.reason: This is keyed component insertion and retention on a moving robot wrist. The candidate does not install a component; it unlocks, tunes, relocks, and validates an already mounted damper through impacts. Generic alignment and retention are insufficient to establish overlap. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift limits are incompletely specified.

comparisons.objective: Commission a shock absorber versus brake a coasting flywheel before removing its hub nut.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine tool engagement and response-based adjustment versus lever braking followed by nut removal and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Two controlled impacts without bottoming versus wheel speed below 0.15 rad/s, nut in tray, brake reset, and no hand near the moving rim.
comparisons.reason: Both concern moving machinery and safe isolation, but the tested manipulation and endpoint differ. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift limits are not numeric.

comparisons.objective: Tune a damper versus route two robot-axis cables and latch a cable carrier.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key/collar adjustment and repeated cycling versus bimanual cable routing, ordering, and twelve snap-latch closures.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeatable impact absorption with lock retention versus every carrier link covered and latched, cables uncrossed, and strain relief not displaced over 5 mm.
comparisons.reason: The record tests deformable routing and repeated latching, not dynamic commissioning. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift thresholds remain unspecified.

comparisons.objective: Commission a compact damper versus lower a hoisted motor onto four studs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-tool unlocking and fine rotary adjustment versus bimanual pendant actuation, load steering, and multi-stud alignment.
comparisons.success_condition: Two safe carriage stops versus all feet flat over studs, chain slack, hands released, and no under-load, pinch, or high-speed stud strike event.
comparisons.reason: Both involve industrial equipment and physical control actuation, but their tested abilities are materially different. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift limits are undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Use a prepared two-jaw screw puller to extract a fitted collar, recover it in a tray, and park the intact tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Counterhold a loose puller while repeatedly turning and regrasping its screw, then bimanually transfer, spread jaws, release the collar, and place the tool.
comparisons.success_condition: Collar clears the shaft after measured screw rotation, remains in the tray, and the intact puller rests within tight pose tolerances for two seconds with hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Although both tasks include bimanual stabilization and rotary tool manipulation, this record tests forceful extraction, recovered-part handling, jaw spreading, and tool parking. The candidate tests fine damping adjustment, setscrew locking, and retained dynamic stopping performance; the shared primitives do not amount to the same ability. Candidate rebound, overload, and post-lock drift thresholds remain numerically incomplete.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus align and cut a card with a guillotine cutter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine tool/collar adjustment versus bimanual card registration, hold-down, and controlled blade actuation with hand clearance.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeatable non-bottoming stops versus card alignment within 5 mm, completed cut, blade left down, and no hand in the hazard zone.
comparisons.reason: The tasks share only guarded actuation and safety discipline. Candidate overload, rebound, and drift thresholds are not numerically declared.

comparisons.objective: Candidate tunes and locks a robot-axis damper through repeated impact tests; pr-1760 assembles and pulses a mini chopper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, setscrew unlocking/relocking, fine collar adjustment, and response-driven iteration. pr-1760 requires blade placement, bayonet alignment/twist locking, bowl counterholding, and button pressing.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe stops within the damper’s energy, velocity, and 12 mm stroke limits, with no hard-stop strike, rebound, overload, or setting drift. pr-1760 requires one pulse with the blade seated, lid locked, blade untouched, bowl stable, and arms returned.
comparisons.reason: Both include rotational locking and control actuation, but they test different mechanisms and outcomes: dynamic energy-absorption commissioning versus appliance assembly/interlock operation. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift thresholds are not fully numeric, but that omission does not create a plausible duplicate.

comparisons.objective: Candidate commissions an adjustable shock absorber; pr-1870 removes a drawer from its slides and sets it down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a hex key and fine collar rotation, then evaluates impacts. pr-1870 simultaneously operates opposite-sense release levers while pulling, supporting, lowering, and releasing a large drawer.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate must retain an adjustment that produces two non-bottoming controlled stops. pr-1870 requires the drawer off both slides, flat and still on the table, with grippers clear; versions additionally record simultaneous lever operation or rely on physical latch blocking.
comparisons.reason: The drawer task tests simultaneous bilateral latch release and load extraction, not parameter adjustment, tool use, or dynamic stopping response.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock a shock absorber versus set and lock a telescoping gauge to a bore diameter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve fine mechanical adjustment and lock retention; the record additionally requires sweeping the gauge through a bore and extracting it without changing span.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate tests repeated dynamic stopping and witness-torque retention; record tests span within 0.10 mm and released placement on a stand.
comparisons.reason: The shared set-and-lock primitive is generic; dynamic response tuning is a meaningfully different tested ability from dimensional transfer. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift thresholds are missing.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus place three devices on matching charging locations.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool alignment, collar tuning, and relocking versus varied object placement, magnetic alignment, and flexible-watch handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Two qualified physical stops versus all three released devices continuously charging for five seconds while the stand stays within 5 mm/5 degrees.
comparisons.reason: The physical interactions and functional verification differ substantially. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift tolerances remain unspecified.

comparisons.objective: Tune a shock absorber versus fill and strike three drywall holes flush.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hex-key and rotary adjustment versus loading, spreading, and scraping modeled spackle with a putty knife.
comparisons.success_condition: Repeatable safe impacts with setting retention versus all holes filled within 0.3 mm, proud area at most 10 mm², and knife set down.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective or manipulation overlap exists beyond tool handling. Candidate overload, rebound, and drift thresholds are undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Candidate tunes and locks a damper; pr-270 identifies and replaces the correctly rated fuse in a named DIN-rail holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires hex-key insertion, counterholding, fine adjustment, locking, and iterative cycling. pr-270 requires opening a hinged carrier, extracting and inserting a small cartridge, selecting the correct spare, reclosing, and passing a pull test.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate succeeds through repeatable impact behavior and retained setting. pr-270 requires the KTK-6 seated in F2, the blown fuse in the tray, F2 closed and pull-test secure, while wrong-holder opening or KTK-10 insertion zeros the score.
comparisons.reason: Small-part manipulation is shared only generically. Fuse selection/replacement and carrier retention test a different ability from adjustment of damping based on measured motion.

comparisons.objective: Commission a damper versus depanel and tray a circuit board.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine tool/collar adjustment versus registration over a break edge, bimanual brace-and-bend, controlled fracture, and transfer.
comparisons.success_condition: Two controlled carriage stops versus a valid downward break with tight pose-history constraints and safe board placement in an ESD tray.
comparisons.reason: The record tests controlled separation and handling, not tuning or retention. Candidate overload, rebound, and drift limits remain undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Candidate commissions a mechanical damper; pr-996 calibrates a colorimeter with a blank and measures a sealed sample at a requested wavelength.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate performs tool-mediated unlocking, collar tuning, and physical impact cycling. pr-996 identifies, orients, seats, and returns cuvettes while operating wavelength, calibration, and lid controls.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe physical stops and lock retention. pr-996 requires a valid reference-dependent absorbance record within 0.02 AU, correct orientation and wavelength, and both cuvettes returned, released, and still; loss can zero the score.
comparisons.reason: The colorimeter task tests reference-dependent analytical sequencing and vessel orientation, not force-response tuning or mechanical setting retention.

comparisons.objective: Tune and lock a shock absorber versus orient and clamp an angle-grinder guard.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require stabilizing equipment, releasing a clamp, rotating a component, and reclamping; candidate uniquely uses a hex key and iterative dynamic feedback.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two acceptable impacts plus a post-lock drift test; record requires guard direction within 30 degrees, lever flat, grinder unmoved, and hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Despite substantial shared adjustment primitives, the record tests a prescribed static orientation while the candidate tests dynamic commissioning from observed response. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift thresholds remain numerically undeclared.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts a robot-axis shock absorber; pr-1837 clips a pulse oximeter fully onto a manikin’s index finger without dragging the hand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a hex key, counterhold, fine collar rotation, and iterative test cycles. pr-1837 squeezes and holds a spring clip open, aligns and slides it over a finger, releases it to clamp, and steadies a loose hand bimanually.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two non-bottoming, non-overloaded stops with no drift. pr-1837 requires the correctly oriented clip seated near its finger stop, clamped and released, with the hand within displacement limits; excessive hand motion or a fallen device zeros the trial.
comparisons.reason: Spring-clip placement on a supported target tests sustained aperture control and insertion, whereas the candidate tests adjustable damping and retained calibration.

comparisons.objective: Tune a shock absorber versus select conveyor parts and assemble a pictured model.
